title: Add structured response mode with error codes and stream preservation for OpenAI compatibility
author: Aisha Raman
commits: 7f1c3d4 - add response_mode enum and transport-layer hooks for schema negotiation
3b9a8ff - plumb schema validation error codes through openai-compat shim
a2d5e11 - preserve streaming buffers on partial schema failures and add tests
c0b2f47 - update docs, examples, and SDK compatibility notes
description: Motivation: Provide a developer-facing structured response mode that 1) preserves streaming behavior for large responses, 2) surfaces deterministic schema validation error codes for programmatic handling, and 3) remains compatible with the OpenAI-style response_format and function/tool calling patterns. This PR introduces a 'structured_response_mode' enum (lenient|strict|best_effort), standardizes error codes emitted on schema validation failures, and modifies the streaming adapter to buffer and emit partial, reparsable fragments when strict mode cannot be satisfied. Key design goals: maintain low-latency streaming for large outputs, give callers machine-friendly error signals (e.g., ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, ERR_REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING), and allow SDKs to opt into strict enforcement. Changes: - Add response_mode and schema negotiation handshake to inference API surface - Implement schema_validator with machine-readable error codes and short, stable messages - Extend openai_compat stream_adapter to support buffer preservation and rewind on schema fallback - Add python SDK helpers to choose behavior and translate error codes into exceptions/wrappers - Add integration tests for streaming + structured output + function calling - Update docs with migration guidance and examples Checklist: - [x] API definition + handshake implemented - [x] Runtime schema validator and error codes - [x] Streaming adapter buffer preservation implemented - [x] SDK gating + examples added - [x] Integration tests added and passing - [x] Docs updated How to test locally: run tests/integration/test_structured_output_streaming.py which spins a lightweight mock model and asserts streaming fragments are preserved when switching from strict to best_effort. Linear: ENG-1127 tracks runtime work; PM-341 covers product acceptance criteria. Related: builds on prior schema negotiation work (see PR 31206) but diverges by adding explicit error codes and a streaming buffer-preserve strategy.
review_comments: Diego Marquez: Important improvement. Can we make the error code enum stable across releases? Also request small refactor in schema_validator to separate validation and message formatting.
Aisha Raman: Agreed on stable enum. Extracted ValidationResult -> crate schema_error_codes and added unit tests to lock codes. Refactor applied in commit 3b9a8ff.
Lena Hofstad: Streaming buffer preserve approach looks good but I'm concerned about memory growth for very long streams. Suggest a cap + eviction policy and a metric.
Aisha Raman: Added a soft cap and a metric (structured_output.replay_buffer_bytes) and evict-oldest policy; documented in observability changes. See commit a2d5e11.
Marcus Li: CI flaked on the integration test once (timeout). Reran CI. Tests passed on rerun. Please add a longer timeout to the flaky test.
Aisha Raman: Increased timeout and added retry hook in test harness. CI green on rerun.
Diego Marquez: Approving pending docs clarification on migration path for existing OpenAI-compatible clients.
Aisha Raman: Added migration section and examples in console/docs/structured-response-mode.md. Marking as ready.
release_notes: Adds structured_response_mode (lenient|strict|best_effort) to the inference API; introduces stable schema validation error codes (ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, ERR_REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING, ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH); improves streaming adapter to preserve partial buffers and allow graceful fallback from strict to best_effort. SDKs updated to expose the toggle and translate codes into exceptions/wrappers. See docs/structured-response-mode.md for migration steps.
